entities.summary:
Eudorus of Alexandria was an ancient Greek philosopher and a representative of Middle Platonism.

Born in Alexandria, Egypt, around 150 BCE, Eudorus was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic world, renowned for his efforts to reconstruct Plato's philosophy in terms of Pythagoreanism. His ideas had a significant impact on the development of Western philosophy, particularly in the areas of epistemology and metaphysics.

Eudorus' philosophical works were highly respected during his lifetime, and his legacy continued to shape the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. His ideas influenced later philosophers, such as Plotinus and Porphyry, and remain an important part of the Middle Platonist tradition.

Despite the passage of time, Eudorus' contributions to philosophy remain relevant, offering insights into the complex and nuanced nature of knowledge and reality. His work continues to be studied by scholars and philosophers today, providing a window into the intellectual currents of ancient Greece.
